title: September 2001: Evidence, Institutions, and Policy
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
On 11 September 2001, nineteen al-Qaeda operatives hijacked four passenger aircraft in the United States. Two aircraft struck the towers of the World Trade Center, one struck the Pentagon, and passengers and crew resisted on the fourth before it crashed in Pennsylvania. Nearly three thousand victims were killed. A careful account begins with verified events and respects the difference between evidence and later speculation.

The national commission created to investigate the attacks concluded that the country was unprepared. Relevant fragments of information existed, but agencies faced barriers in collection, analysis, sharing, imagination, and coordinated action. This does not mean that every warning clearly predicted the complete plot. *Hindsight bias* can make scattered clues look more obvious after the outcome is known. The harder question is which institutional changes could have connected signals without producing unlimited surveillance or constant false alarms.

The United States and other governments then made many policy choices: military action in Afghanistan against al-Qaeda and the Taliban government that sheltered it, new security laws and screening systems, intelligence reorganization, and the creation of the Department of Homeland Security. These responses should be assessed separately. A later policy may have been justified, ineffective, harmful, or contested; its occurrence after the attack does not by itself prove necessity.

The 2003 invasion of Iraq must also be distinguished from responsibility for the 2001 attacks. The commission reported no evidence that Iraq directed the operation. More broadly, counterterrorism creates a continuing design problem: authorities must connect information quickly enough to prevent violence while preserving legal review, privacy, equal treatment, and the ability to correct mistaken suspicion. Security and liberty are not solved by slogans; they require institutions that can measure both missed threats and harmful false positives.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Every later security policy was a necessary consequence of the attacks.

options.label: B
options.text: No useful information existed before the attacks.

options.label: C
options.text: Facts, institutional failures, and later policy choices must be examined as related but distinct layers.

options.label: D
options.text: Iraq directed the 2001 operation.

questions.answer: 正解：C。本文は確認事実、事前の制度的失敗、事件後の個別政策を関連づけつつ区別します。Aは後続政策を必然化し、Bは断片情報を否定し、Dは委員会の認定と反対です。

questions.prompt: Why does paragraph 1 distinguish verified events from later speculation?

options.label: A
options.text: To ground responsibility and policy evaluation in checkable evidence rather than later political or conspiratorial claims

options.label: B
options.text: To suggest that verified facts are less respectful to victims than dramatic stories

options.label: C
options.text: To treat every later claim as equally reliable

options.label: D
options.text: To avoid identifying any documented event or actor

questions.answer: 正解：A。責任帰属と政策評価を確認可能な事実に置き、後世の政治的主張や根拠の弱い推測から分けるためです。被害者への敬意も刺激性より検証可能性を優先することにあります。

questions.prompt: Which definition is closest to “hindsight bias”?

options.label: A
options.text: judging past predictability as greater after learning the outcome

options.label: B
options.text: refusing to use any historical evidence

options.label: C
options.text: predicting every future event correctly

options.label: D
options.text: sharing all private data without limits

questions.answer: 正解：A。結果を知った後で、当時の予見可能性を実際より高く感じる偏りです。これは失敗検証を禁じる語ではなく、当時利用できた情報と不確実性を復元するための注意です。

questions.prompt: Why can the commission's finding not be summarized as “there were no warnings”?

options.label: A
options.text: Information fragments existed, but they were not adequately collected, interpreted, shared, or converted into coordinated action.

options.label: B
options.text: Every fragment clearly described the complete plot in advance.

options.label: C
options.text: Agencies had no barriers to sharing or analysis.

options.label: D
options.text: The commission concluded that the country was fully prepared.

questions.answer: 正解：A。問題は情報ゼロではなく、断片が完全な計画として統合・共有・行動化されなかったことです。Bは警告の明確さを誇張し、C・Dは委員会の結論と逆です。

questions.prompt: Why should post-attack policies be evaluated separately?

options.label: A
options.text: Military action, laws, screening, and reorganization had different aims, evidence, effects, side effects, and legal grounds.

options.label: B
options.text: Their shared timing automatically proves that all were necessary.

options.label: C
options.text: Every policy had identical goals and consequences.

options.label: D
options.text: A harmful policy becomes justified whenever it follows an attack.

questions.answer: 正解：A。軍事行動、法制度、検査、組織再編は目的・根拠・効果・副作用・法的基礎が異なります。事件後という時間的共通性だけで一括正当化できず、B～Dはpost hocの飛躍です。

questions.prompt: How does the passage distinguish the military actions in Afghanistan and Iraq?

options.label: A
options.text: Afghanistan was described as action against al-Qaeda and the Taliban government that sheltered it, while the commission found no evidence that Iraq directed the 2001 operation.

options.label: B
options.text: The commission concluded that Iraq planned and directed the attacks.

options.label: C
options.text: Neither action had any relationship to later policy choices.

options.label: D
options.text: The Taliban government was described as directing Iraq's 2003 invasion.

questions.answer: 正解：A。アフガニスタンでの行動はアルカイダと保護したタリバン政権への対応として説明されますが、委員会はイラクが2001年の作戦を指示した証拠を認めていません。

questions.prompt: Why must a security system measure false positives as well as missed threats?

options.label: A
options.text: Lowering the detection threshold may catch more threats but can wrongly target uninvolved people and harm liberty, equality, and resource allocation.

options.label: B
options.text: Only false positives matter because missed threats cause no harm.

options.label: C
options.text: A system can always reduce both errors to zero without trade-offs.

options.label: D
options.text: Wrongly labeling innocent people improves the reliability of intelligence.

questions.answer: 正解：A。検出閾値を下げれば見逃しを減らせても、無関係な人を脅威と誤認し、自由・平等・資源配分を害し得ます。制度精度は片方の誤差だけでは評価できません。

questions.prompt: What causal warning is expressed by “Its occurrence after the attack does not by itself prove necessity”?

options.label: A
options.text: Temporal sequence alone does not establish that a later policy was required or caused by the only possible response.

options.label: B
options.text: Any policy adopted later was necessarily effective.

options.label: C
options.text: Events occurring after an attack can never be evaluated.

options.label: D
options.text: The attack and every later policy are the same event.

questions.answer: 正解：A。「その政策が攻撃後に起きたという事実だけでは、その必要性は証明されない」。時間的順序を因果的必然へ変えるpost hocの誤りを避け、代替案と個別成果を評価します。

questions.prompt: Which institutional design best balances information sharing with civil liberties?

options.label: A
options.text: Purpose-limited sharing under auditable rules, proportionate and time-limited collection, independent review, correction routes, and measures of both missed threats and false positives

options.label: B
options.text: Unlimited collection, permanent retention, and no legal review

options.label: C
options.text: No information sharing under any circumstances

options.label: D
options.text: Performance measures that count only successful detections and conceal mistaken suspicion

questions.answer: 正解：A。目的、監査可能なアクセス、比例性、期限、独立審査、誤記録の訂正、両種の誤差測定を組み合わせます。無制限データは雑音、差別、過信を生み得るため、B～Dは信頼性と権利を両立しません。
